name: SPHEREx
full_name: Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization and Ices Explorer
summary: NASA all-sky near-infrared spectral-survey satellite. Alongside primary science on cosmic origins and ices, line-intensity mapping can test eV-scale ALP-dark-matter decay.
detection_principle: All-sky low-resolution spectra form intensity maps that can be cross-correlated with galaxy or lensing structure to separate astrophysical lines from hypothetical ALP-decay photons.

status.label: Operation supported by evidence
status.evidence: NASA's current page labels it an “Active Mission,” launched in 2025; dark-matter papers are forecasts, not existing discoveries.

timeline.event: Launch, using the local date on NASA's page

results.summary: Line-intensity-mapping and structure-cross-correlation papers forecast dark-matter sensitivity; these are not measured upper limits.

science_scope: Constrains dark-matter distribution and properties through gravity, microlensing or structure statistics; does not directly identify dark-matter particles.
